conviction_note: Regions has told the market almost everything about this quarter: Q3 NII up about 2%, NIM stable to modestly higher, fees and capital markets at the low end, all in its Aug-Sep 8-K deck. Nothing new came from the company after that (no intra-quarter 8-K, and I found no Barclays transcript). So the evidence is peer read-through. Southeast and national peers that printed this week show funding costs rising: First Horizon's interest-bearing deposit cost rose 12bp, FB Financial's 7bp, and PNC's NII grew 2% against its own 3-3.5% guide. Credit at those peers is benign. Findings sum to -0.65. The scaled number is 45% up on a 3.0% absolute move, which gives -0.3. The two measurements agree in sign. The lean is small because it rests on proxies, it agrees with a skew that already pays for downside, and RF's reaction history is damped (median 1.31%) and sold the July beat (-2.31% on $0.68 vs $0.63).
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $0.66: TickerLeague, 10 analysts, range $0.63-0.68 (https://tickerleague.com/companies/RF/estimates). Benzinga also shows $0.66 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RF/earnings-forecasts) and Earnings Whispers $0.67 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/RF). Revenue $1.98-1.99B (Benzinga, Earnings Whispers). Company bar: Q3 NII about +2% q/q, NIM stable to modestly higher than 2Q26's 3.66%, adjusted NIR toward the low end of FY +3-5%, capital markets $90-105M per quarter trending to the low end in 3Q. FY26 NCOs 40-50bp, FY26 NII +2.5-4%, NIM exit ~3.70%. Source: Regions 8-K investor deck, Aug-Sep 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001281761/000128176126000057/a3q26investormeetingmate.htm). The bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources, so no cap applies.
positioning_check: Short interest is moderate, not crowded. June 30, 2026 settlement: 53.9M shares, ~8.35% of float, 4.44 days to cover (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RF/short-interest). Mid-August snapshot: 52.1M, 6.1% of float, 4.8 days (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/RF). I found no September settlement. Options: 25-delta skew +3.43 vol points (downside paid), put/call open-interest ratio 3.48, ATM IV 32.4% against 20-day realised vol of 17.2%, event-implied move 6.31% from the baseline. The implied move looks inflated by IV elevated across the 36-day expiry: RF's own median reaction is 1.31% and its maximum 6.12%. Tape: spot $27.33, run-up -4.04% over 20 days, -15.65% from the 52-week high. The CFO's fractional Form 4 sale on 2026-09-10 printed at $29.895, so the stock is down ~8.6% since then.

findings.finding: Two Southeast peers that reported Q3 2026 this week show deposit costs rising in a quarter when the policy rate was flat until a 16 Sept hike. First Horizon (Memphis; overlaps Regions in TN, MS, AL, FL), 15 Oct: interest-bearing deposit cost 2.45%, up 12bp q/q, on higher customer deposit costs and new-account promotions; NIM 3.48%, down 1bp. FB Financial (Nashville), 13 Oct: interest-bearing deposit cost 2.88%, up 7bp; NIM 3.83%, down 12bp, 'higher funding costs outpacing earning-asset yields'. The bar this hits is Regions' guide of NIM stable to modestly higher than 3.66%, NII up ~2%, built on mid/high-30s deposit betas. In 2Q26 Regions' interest-bearing deposit cost fell 3bp to 1.69%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RF's NII/NIM line drives its prints. 2Q26 beat ($0.68 vs $0.63) with NIM 3.66% and still fell -2.31% on 2026-07-17. 4Q25 EPS missed ($0.57 vs $0.61) and fell -2.63% on 2026-01-16. Reactions are damped: median |move| 1.31% over 7 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: First Horizon released this morning (15 Oct) and FB Financial on 13 Oct. Regions' sell-side bar was set off its own NIM-up guide. If the street had marked Regions' NIM down for peer funding costs, the consensus would sit below the ~2% NII guide and previews would mention deposit-cost risk. I found no Q3 2026 preview discussing it. Partly priced: the skew pays for downside and the stock is down ~8.6% since 10 Sept.
findings.independence: FB Financial's 8-K is a separate document pointing the same way (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000063/a3q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm, 2026-10-13). Counter-evidence: Home BancShares (Arkansas) interest-bearing deposit cost fell 2bp to 2.37% and its NIM rose to 4.53% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001331520/000133152026000117/homb093026earningsrelease.htm). Regions' deposit base is more retail and non-interest-bearing (low-30s% of deposits) than either FHN's or FBK's. This is a proxy: neither peer is Regions' own number.

findings.finding: Large-bank NII came in light this week as funding costs rose. PNC's Q3 2026 NII grew $99M (+2%) q/q against its own guide of +3-3.5%; NIM fell 2bp to 2.94% on 'higher funding costs', and non-interest-bearing deposits slipped from 23% to 22% of the total. Wells Fargo's Q3 NII of ~$12.52B was slightly below a ~$12.59B forecast, with higher deposit costs and a modest decline in non-interest-bearing deposits named. Regions guided Q3 NII +~2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as the deposit-cost finding: RF sold its 2Q26 beat at -2.31% and fell -2.63% on the 4Q25 miss. The WFC pre-market reaction to its NII miss was reported as -1.1%; I found no close.
findings.why_not_priced: PNC printed this morning, after every RF estimate was set. If priced, RF's NII estimate would already sit below the ~2% guide. Partly priced through the sector tape and the put skew.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo Q3 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000072971/000007297126000318/wfc3qer10-13x26ex991xrelea.htm, 2026-10-13) is a different document. It shares a mechanism (funding cost) with the Southeast deposit-cost finding but rests on different numbers. National banks have different deposit mixes from Regions, so this is a proxy and sized below the Southeast finding.

findings.finding: Peer credit is benign this week. PNC's annualised NCO ratio was 0.28%, including $35M from a student-loan transfer to held-for-sale, and its provision was flat at $189M. First Horizon's NCOs were 22bp (20bp in Q2), and its provision ex the mortgage sale was $20M. FB Financial's NCOs were 4bp. Regions guides FY26 NCOs to 40-50bp, and 2Q26 printed 0.42% with criticized and non-performing loans shrinking. That supports an RF NCO print at the low end of the guide and possibly a reserve release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2Q26 credit improved (NCOs down 12bp to 0.42%) and the stock still fell -2.31%. On this name credit beats have not been paid.
findings.why_not_priced: The finding lands inside the company's 40-50bp guide, so the market was told to expect it. That is why it is sized near zero. It carries some weight only because the October 2025 regional-bank credit scare made credit the line the sector's tails come from.
findings.independence: First Horizon (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000178/a3q2026earningsrelease.htm) and FB Financial (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000063/a3q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm) are separate documents. FHN's release also appears in the Southeast deposit-cost finding, but this finding reads a different line of it.

findings.finding: Capital markets were weak at a peer this quarter. PNC's capital markets and advisory revenue fell 25% q/q ($577M to $433M) and its fee income fell 6%. Regions already guided capital markets to the low end of $90-105M in 3Q and adjusted NIR to the low end of FY +3-5%, citing market volatility and elevated rates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No attributed reaction to RF's fee line in the baseline. 2Q26 adjusted NIR rose 7% q/q and the stock fell -2.31%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It lands inside Regions' own low-end guide, so it is sized near zero. It is filed because a fee shortfall below the low end would compound a NIM miss.
findings.independence: The Regions 8-K deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001281761/000128176126000057/a3q26investormeetingmate.htm) carries the guide. PNC's release is shared with the national NII and peer-credit findings, but this finding reads a different line.

findings.finding: The rate regime turned during the quarter. The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sept 2026, Regions Bank raised prime to 7.00% effective 17 Sept, and PNC's Q3 baseline assumes two more hikes (Dec 2026, Mar 2027). Regions describes its position as 'mostly neutral', with a mid-30s deposit beta and $3.5B of forward-starting hedges. Whatever it says about a 2027 NII trajectory in a hiking regime is new information, and its sign is ambiguous.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None attributable in the baseline. RF's 2025-07-18 +6.12% reaction is its largest and came with an outlook print, but no line was sourced for it.
findings.why_not_priced: Regions' guide predates the hike. The skew and the elevated IV suggest the market prices a wider outcome on the forward outlook than RF's history shows. Neutral rate positioning leaves the sign open, so the finding is sized at zero with a wide band.
findings.independence: The prime-rate change was reported on Regions' newsroom and aggregators (search result, finviz/businesswire listing). The Fed hike is reported by PNC's Zacks preview and by https://therighttrader.com/economic-calendar/fomc. Regions' neutral-position language comes from the 2Q26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001281761/000128176126000050/rf-2026630xexhibitx992.htm).

findings.finding: A Southeast peer took a large balance-sheet action this quarter. First Horizon booked a $473M pre-tax loss on a pending sale of ~$4.5B of low-yield consumer mortgages, calling it accretive going forward. Regions took a $40M securities-repositioning loss in 2Q26, so a further repositioning excluded from adjusted EPS is plausible. Nothing from Regions confirms one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2Q26 carried the $40M repositioning loss and the stock fell -2.31%. The loss was excluded from adjusted EPS and was not the attributed driver.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference with no Regions document behind it. It sits below operating income, has no stated path to the guide, and is sized at zero.
findings.independence: Regions 2Q26 $40M repositioning (https://www.panabee.com/news/regions-financial-earnings-q2-2026-report). This uses the same FHN document as the deposit-cost finding, but a different line.

findings.finding: The downside is already partly paid for. Put/call open interest is 3.48, the highest in the window per the sweep. The 25-delta skew is +3.43 vol points. The stock is down ~8.6% since the CFO's 10 Sept Form 4 print at $29.895, -4.04% over 20 days and -15.65% from its 52-week high. Short interest is a moderate 6-8% of float at 4.4-4.8 days to cover, so this is hedging rather than a crowded short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of RF's last 7 prints, 4 rose. Every move was within ±2.7% except +6.12% in July 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. A small offset against the negative proxies: a heavily hedged name that prints inside guide can relieve upward. Sized small because the drawdown has no sourced company-specific cause.
findings.independence: Benzinga short interest (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RF/short-interest). The options numbers come from the sealed baseline.

baseline_tension: What I found leans the same way as the skew (+3.43, downside paid) and the 20-day drawdown, so it is probably partly priced. The positioning finding and RF's damped reaction history pull p_up toward 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (proxy) and rule 7 (sign agrees with the skew, so partly priced): Southeast deposit-cost finding -0.7 to -0.6.
Rule 5: national-bank NII finding -0.4 to -0.3. These are big banks with a different deposit mix from Regions.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is not a cause): positioning finding +0.3 to +0.15.
Rules 1, 2 and 6 left the rest standing. The credit and fee findings were already near zero as inside-guide; the repositioning one_off was already 0. Scaled number unchanged at p_up 45, abs 3.0.
